# Collinear marker connector

Use when an ARC grid has a uniform background and sparse marker cells, and demonstrations show connector-colored cells appearing along straight rows or columns between markers.

## Rule established for task-63e6a38f
Preserve all original cells and insert color 3 into background cells strictly between aligned pairs of same-color markers in a common row or column. Markers are endpoints and remain unchanged. Use all same-color marker alignments; a line with multiple markers is partitioned by consecutive markers, and each gap is filled. Do not extend past the outermost endpoint, fill diagonals, globally recolor the background, or connect different marker colors. Adjacent endpoints need no inserted cells.

Evidence across the three demos: demo 1 had background 6 and marker color 5; output color 3 traced horizontal and vertical gaps between aligned 5 markers while leaving background outside marker endpoints unchanged. Demo 2 had background 9, markers 1, and likewise filled gaps with 3, retaining marker cells and unrelated background. Demo 3 used background 5 and marker 7, with the same connector color 3 and horizontal/vertical gap fills. In the accepted test, color-8 markers at row 1, columns 12 and 14 caused only the intervening cell (row 1, column 13) to become 3; all other cells were unchanged.

## Confirmed recurring variant: task-041f67cf
This variant uses sparse same-color markers on a uniform background and inserts color 2 strictly between consecutive aligned markers, preserving marker endpoints and all other cells. Demo: in each row of a 25x4 grid, color-4 markers at columns 0 and 2 had the intervening color-7 cell changed to 2; rows without marker pairs were unchanged. Accepted test: background 6, markers 8; row 4 had markers at columns 5, 7, 9, so columns 6 and 8 became 2; row 13 had markers at columns 2 and 4, so column 3 became 2. Everything else stayed unchanged. This supports connecting consecutive aligned same-color markers horizontally and vertically with color 2; do not extend beyond endpoints. Infer palette from current demos, as connector color varies by task variant.

## Confirmed recurring variant: task-381e5135
The sparse color-3 markers in a mostly color-6 field identify horizontal/vertical gaps, filled with color 2. Preserve all original cells, including all marker 3s and background; only fill cells strictly between consecutive aligned markers. Demo: background 6, markers 3, connector 2. Horizontal row 7 markers at columns 0,1,2 and 6: fill columns 3-5; row 11 markers at columns 0 and 6: fill columns 1-5; row 12 markers at columns 0,2,4,6: fill columns 1,3,5. Vertical alignments include col0 markers rows 7,10,11 (fill rows 8-9 between 7 and 10), and col6 markers rows 7,9,11 (fill rows 8 and 10). In the 30x27 test (background 7, marker 5, connector 2), this rule was accepted; same behavior with palette inferred from current demo. Note missing cells in col19/25 or row23 are not bridged unless there are aligned marker endpoints on both sides. Do not extend beyond endpoints or fill arbitrary enclosed-region/background gaps.

## task-381e5135 generated variants and unresolved instance (2026-09)
Do not assume this task ID always means straight collinear connector fills. It has multiple variants. The classic marker-connector recurrence is separately confirmed: same-color sparse markers in rows/columns have only intervening background cells filled with connector color 2. However, the current failed 24x21 test had demos from several structures and all 8 submissions were wrong; none of the guesses below are validated output.

Current instance demos (palette varies) reveal a common operation of changing selected background-colored cells to 2 along selected rows/columns, but plain interpolation between consecutive same-color markers does not account for all cells:
- Pair 1, 8x27, bg8, markers4. Row2 gaps changed to2 at c4,6,9,11,14,22,25; row6 at c4,8,17,21,23,25. Vertical changes at (r5,c2), (r4,c26),(r5,c26). Marker cells preserved.
- Pair 2, 13x15, bg8, markers0. Changes: row0 c1,c3-6; col1 r1-2,r4-5,r8-9; col7 r4-5,r9; row10 c5-6. Not all aligned marker gaps are filled.
- Pair 3, 21x18, bg1, markers0. Changed to2 at (r1,c11),(r2,c6),(r5,c6),(r6,c6), isolated vacancies on marker-lines; top/bottom horizontal zero bars unchanged.
- Pair 4, 18x29, bg6, markers3. Row2 changed at c9,c12-15; col7 at r5-6,r9-10,r12,r14; col16 at r4,r9,r11,r13-14; row15 at c10,c12-13,c15. This resembles filling missing phase positions on selected lines.
- Pair 5, 15x15, bg5, markers0. Changes: row6 c6-10; col2 r10-13; col11 r7,r10-13; row14 c4-7,c9-10. Could reflect repeated-line/motif completion; rule unresolved.
- Pair 6, 14x22, bg3, frame-like color5 at rows0,10 and cols16,19,21. Only existing 5s changed at (r2,c21),(r6,c21),(r8,c19).
- Pair 7, 9x16, bg9, markers4. Changes to2 at (r2,c12-13),(r3-4,c9,c12,c14),(r7,c12). Existing markers preserved; suggests partial motif completion but exact rule unresolved.

Test was 24x21, bg8/marker1, with top row patterned markers, sparse vertical marker runs at c1 and c16, and bottom row20 with a left run plus scattered markers. All 8 submissions failed. Tried hypotheses included filling collinear gaps, selected vertical/horizontal gap interpolation, and several unions of those fills. Do not reuse any submitted grid. Correct line/mask/periodic completion rule is unresolved. On recurrence, enumerate exact diffs and investigate row/column motif phase completion, testing all changed and preserved cells before submission; do not assume all collinear marker pairs connect.

## Application and validation
1. Copy the input grid.
2. Infer background and marker colors from the current instance's demos; connector color was 3 in the observed task variant.
3. For every row and column, gather marker positions in sorted order.
4. Between consecutive marker positions, change only intervening background cells to the connector color.
5. Preserve markers and all cells outside gaps. Validate dimensions and palette.

Infer the palette from current demos; do not assume colors remain fixed on task-ID recurrence unless confirmed. Keep the strict action-JSON output protocol in ARC stream tasks.

## Additional unresolved task-381e5135 variant (2026-09; do not reuse failed outputs)
This is a separate generated variant from the confirmed straight-connector case above. Three demos used background / marker / connector palettes (4/6/no changes; 1/7/2; 7/6/2). The second and third demos have selected background gaps converted to 2, but a simple rule of connecting every same-color marker pair in each row/column is not sufficient: extensive test outputs based on that assumption all failed. Treat this variant as unresolved.

Demo 1 (16x18): color-6 rectangular outline on color-4 field (top edge row 1 cols 0-8, bottom row 14 cols 0-8, sides col0 and col8 rows2-13) remained entirely unchanged. This is an important preserved-frame negative example.

Note that not every visual line/candidate gap was changed; identify an additional selector before applying a line-connector hypothesis.
Demo 3 (20x24), bg7, marker6, connector2: exact changed cells (0-indexed): row1 c5,c6,c9,c10,c12; row3 c13; row6 c0; row7 c7; rows8-9 c0; row10 c4. Preserved cells include many other marker-like partial lines. Top/bottom partial horizontal bars and repeated vertical segments yield localized gap fills, but the selection rule is not settled from the three examples.

Test was 28x19, bg9, marker8, with sparse markers: col4 at rows2,3,4,6,8,9,13,17,19, plus row23 c4-7; col15 markers rows2,6,10,12,18; and extra marker at row23 c11. Eight submissions were incorrect. Most guesses over-connected apparent collinear markers, filling col4 gaps/ranges and/or col15 gaps, and failed; do not use their proposed grids as evidence.
